verses.text: Around that time the Philistines gathered their armies to fight Israel. Achish told David, “You and your men will be going out with me in the army.”
David answered, “Then you'll see what your servant can do.” Achish said, “Then I'll make you my bodyguard for life.”
Samuel had died, and all Israel had mourned him and buried him in his hometown of Ramah. Saul had driven the mediums and spiritists out of the land.
The Philistines gathered and camped at Shunem. Saul gathered all Israel, and they camped at Gilboa.
When Saul saw the Philistine army, he was terrified and his heart shook.
Saul asked the LORD for guidance, but the LORD didn't answer him through dreams, the Urim, or the prophets.
Saul told his servants, “Find me a woman who can speak with the dead so I can go and consult her.” His servants said, “There's a medium at Endor.”
Saul disguised himself in different clothes and went to the woman at night with two men. He asked, “Please consult a spirit for me and bring up whoever I name.”
She answered, “You know what Saul did. He drove out the mediums and spiritists. Why are you setting a trap to get me killed?”
Saul swore to her by the LORD, “As surely as the LORD lives, you won't be punished for this.”
She asked, “Who should I bring up for you?” He answered, “Bring up Samuel.”
When the woman saw Samuel, she screamed. She told Saul, “Why did you trick me? You're Saul!”
The king said, “Don't be afraid. What do you see?” She answered, “I see a god coming up out of the earth.”
He asked what he looked like. She said, “An old man is coming up, wrapped in a robe.” Saul realized it was Samuel and bowed with his face to the ground.

Samuel asked, “Why have you disturbed me by bringing me up?” Saul answered, “I'm in terrible trouble. The Philistines are fighting me and God has left me. He won't answer through prophets or dreams. So I've called you to tell me what to do.”
Samuel said, “Why are you asking me now that the LORD has left you and become your enemy?
The LORD has done just what he said through me. He's torn the kingdom out of your hands and given it to David, your neighbor.
You refused to listen to the LORD and didn't carry out his fierce anger against Amalek. That's why the LORD has done this to you today.
The LORD will hand Israel over to the Philistines along with you. Tomorrow you and your sons will be with me. The LORD will hand Israel's army over to the Philistines too.”
Saul immediately fell flat on the ground, terrified by Samuel's words. He had no strength left because he hadn't eaten anything all day and all night.
The woman came over and saw how distressed he was. She said, “I listened to you and risked my life by doing what you asked.
Now please listen to me. Let me give you something to eat so you have the strength to go on your way.”
Saul refused and said he wouldn't eat. But his servants and the woman kept urging him until he agreed. He got up from the ground and sat on the bed.
The woman had a fattened calf in the house. She quickly slaughtered it, then took flour, kneaded it, and baked bread without yeast.
She served the food to Saul and his servants, and they ate. Then they got up and left that night.
